name: SCHÖNOX AB
paste:
SCHÖNOX® AB: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SCHÖNOX® AB, October 2025, Version 01.08 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/k/schoenox_ab.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SCHÖNOX® AB where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (October 2025, Version 01.08).
1.2 Product description. A crack bridging, waterproof sheet membrane system made of polyethylene covered with a special fleece designed for use in wet areas, balconies and swimming pools.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - • Highly loaded commercial wet areas and kitchens. • Balconies, & terraces prior to tiling.
    - • Swimming pools, commercial aquatic centre pools, spas and sauna's.
    - • Residential wet areas and bathrooms
    - Substrates
    - Schonox AB is suitable on:
    - • Concrete
    - • Masonry brick & blockwork (fully grouted/rendered ) • Cement-based screeds and renders
    - • Fibre Cement Boards and sheets"
    - • Gypsum Plaster Boards*
    - • Sika Approved Acoustic underlays
    - • Light weight Polystyurene boards coated with mortar*
    - * Refer manufacturer instructions and load limits. Boards and sheet shall be specifically designed to receive tiles
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.11.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SCHÖNOX® AB
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: WATERPROOFING SHEET MEMBRANE & CRACK ISOLATION SYSTEM FOR TILE AND STONE INSTALLATIONS
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Certificates and test reports.
    - AS 4858:2004
    - AS 4654.1, 2012
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS4858:2004: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Features (p.1).
    - AS4654.1: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Features (p.1).
    - AS 4858:2004: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - AS 4654.1: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - ASTM E96: cited with a stated property or value. Where: Technical Information > Water-vapour transmission rate (p.2).
    - AS ISO 3958.1: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Application Instructions > Cement mortar beds / Screeds: (p.4).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Extra Heavy Duty - Robinson floor test
    - Highly Flexible, Class III
    - Fast to install
    - Tile & Stone applications may commence as soon as 2 hours after application
    - Suitable over floor heating systems
    - Crack isolation over non-structural cracks up to 6mm
    - Tested and compliant to AS4858:2004 & AS4654.1, 2012
    - Water Vapour retarding
    - Frost Resistant
    - Rotproof
    - Decoupling properties
    - Sheet can be walked on during application
    - Can be used in submerged applications - Seek Sika Specification
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Polyethylene sheet encased with a special fleece.
    - Appearance and colour: Grey or Yellow
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Mass per area: approx, 280g/m²
    - Elongation: Class III, (high elasticity).
    - Tensile strain at break: ≈700%
    - Tensile adhesion strength: Pass, 5.17Mpa
    - Crack bridging ability: 6mm, over non-structural/non dynamic cracks
    - Resistance to UV exposure: 500 hours
    - Water-vapour transmission rate: 0.28g/m²/24hrs (ASTM E96)
    - Service temperature: -20°C to +60°C
2.7 System structure. Wet Areas, Balconies & Terraces; Priming:
    - Seek written Sika Specification for submerged applications such as pools or spas.
    | Porous Substrates | SikaTile 010 Secure Prime |
    | Non-porous Substrates | SikaFloor-14 Prep n Prime |
    | Sheet Membrane System | SikaTile 440 Opti-Cure with Lanko |
    | Schonox AB Adhesive: | latex additive (neat no water added) |
    | Sheet Membrane: | Schonox AB sheet membrane |
    | Sheet Component: | Schonox ST Sealing Tape |
    | Sheet Component: | Schonox ST Corners and Pipe penet- |
    | rations |
    | Tiling System |
    | Tile Adhesive | Any SikaTile tile and stone adhesive |
    | Tile Grout | Any Sika Tile grout |
    | Submerged Applications, Pools Spas, and Saunas |
    (System build-up table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows. Refer to the data sheet (page 3) for the layout.)
    * Refer to all product datasheets for product limitations prior to use.
2.8 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 30 Meter Roll
    - Shelf life: 2+ Years; Refer to the adhesives product data sheet for shelf life information
    - Storage conditions: Store Schonox AB in a dry cool area and horizontal.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (October 2025, Version 01.08) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality - Concrete Floors. Allow 28 days for concrete to cure. Concrete shall be left with an open surface, steel trowel finishes are generally acceptable if they accept water penetration. Wood float finishes are preffered where possible.
3.3 Substrate quality - Cement mortar beds / Screeds.
    - Mortar bed / Screeds must be installed as per AS ISO 3958.1,2007.
    - Application can be undertaken over early aged screeds internally only. Allow screed to dry for a minimum 24 hours at 23°C and 50% relative humidity.
    - Allow screeds to dry and cure externally prior to application.
3.4 Substrate quality - Sheeted substrates. All boards / Underlays must be installed as per manufacturers instructions and specifically designed for tiling.
3.5 Substrate preparation. Prime surfaces prior to application.
    | Application | Primer |
    | Porous Substrates | SikaTile 010 Secure Prime |
    | Non-porous Substrates ie control leak flanges and pipe penetrations | SikaTile 015 Prep N Prime |
    Refer the the primer product data sheet for the complete user instruction prior to use.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (October 2025, Version 01.08) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Effective thickness: 0.55mm
4.3 Mixing ratio. The adhesive used to bond the Schonox AB sheet membrane system: SikaTile 440 Opti-Cure mixed neat with Lanko Latex 751 Additive. Mixing Ratio
    - Additional powder of up to 1kg of SikaTile 440 Opti-Cure may be added to the 5Ltr Lanko Latex 751 to reach your desired consistency.
    - The adhesive may need restirring during its pot life, do not add any additional additive.
    | Application | SikaTile 440 Opti- | LankoLatex 751 | Coverage |
    | Cure |
    | Rollable | 5.5 - 6.25kgs | 5Ltrs | 10m² |
    | Trowelable | 7.0 - 8.0kgs | 5Ltrs | 9m² |
    | Do not dilute the Lanko latex 751 - use neat. |
    | Trowel Application |
    | Trowel size 2.6mm V notched trowel for board substrates |
    | Trowel size 3.5mm V notched trowel for concrete and screed susbstrates Pot Life: |
    | 1.5 hours (approx) |
    | Mixing Instructions: |
    | 1. Add the Lanko latex 751 additive to a clean mixing bucket. |
    | 4. Restir the adhesive for an additional 1 minute then the adhesive can be used. |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    2. Slowly add the SikaTile 440 Opti-Cure to the bucket while stirring with an electric mixing drill.
    3. Mix the adhesive to a smooth lump free mixture and allow the mixture to stand or "slake" for 3 minutes.
4.4 Applied product ready for covering.
    | Substrate | Dry time prior to covering |
    | Porous substrates - wall applications | 12+ hours |
    | Porous substrates - floor applica- | 2+ hours |
    | tions |
    | Non porous substrates and com- | 6+ hours |
    | pressed cement boards |
    | Drying times are measured at 23°C and 50% relative humidity use chart as a guide only. |
    | Hot climate will reduce drying times and cool or cold climate with extend drying times. |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
4.5 Instructions.
    - All Substrates shall be installed as per manufacturers instructions, fit for purpose and designed to handle the loads of a Tile or Stone system.
    - Substrate Deflection: All Substrates under loads must not exceed L/360 for tile and L/720 for Stone.
    - Substrates must be properly cured, structurally sound, free from loose or friable particles, clean, dry and free from contaminates such as dust, dirt, oil, grease, curing compounds, crystaline sealers, laitance, or effloresence.
    - Dependant on the substrate condition and contamination to be removed from the surface, perform adequate scarification, or blast cleaning in order to remove all traces of any materials that could reduce the product adhesion to the substrate.
    - Substrates shall be smooth and continuous without pit, divots. Repair pits or divots with a suitable Sika repair mortar prior to application.
4.6 Equipment.
    - Slow Speed Mixing Drill (Max 500RPM)
    - Plastic trowel / plastic paint scrapers
    - 2.6mm or 3.5mm V notched trowels
    - Paint rollers - 100mm & 230mm
    - Utility knife or scissors
4.7 Application method / tools.
    - Refer to Mixing Ratio section in this document for Adhesive details.
    Application of floor wall functions and corners, Schonox ST Sealing Tape and ST corners
    Apply the adhesive to the substrate junctions with a 100mm roller or v notched trowel. While the adhesive is wet embed the Schonox St Sealing Tape and corners in position
    Apply addition adhesive to overlap the joins and smooth out with a plastic scraper
    Application of Pipe Penetrations - Schonox ST D components
    For PVC fittings, apply a single coat of SikaFloor-14 Prep n Prime and allow to dry.
    For Metal Fittings, lightly abrade with steel wool and then clean residue with Isopropyl Alcohol and allow to dry. Then apply a single coat of SIkaFloor-14 Prep n
    Prime and allow to dry.
    Apply the adhesive around the pipe penetration with the Schonox 100mm roller or a V notched trowel and embed the Schonox ST pipe penetrations and flatten with a plastic scrapper.
    Application of the Sconox Ab Sheet Membrane. Measure and cut sheet as required with the Utility Knife or Scissors
    Apply a layer of the adhesive with a roller or V notched trowel to an area that can be covered prior to adhesive skinning (approx 1m2) and embed the Shonox AB sheet into the adhesive. Immediately fatten the sheet with a plastic scraper. Repeat process by gradually rolling and apply adhesive as required. All sheet joins are to be overlapped by a minimum 50mm and ensure the adhesive covers all sheet joins for a watertight finish.
4.8 Application method / tools - Waterstop Angles, and Terminations.
    - Penetration can be terminated onto the pipe penetrations. Prime PVC pipes with SikaFloor-14 Prep n Prime and allow to dry. Apply the adhesive to the primer and install the Schonox ST D pipe penetrations.
    - Control Leak flanges shall be primed with SikaFloor-14 Prep n Prime and allowed to dry prior to bonding sheet terminations or ST Sealing with the adhesive Waterstop Angles shall be primed with SikaFloor-14 Prep n Prime and allowed to dry. Bond the Schonox ST Sealing tape to Waterstop angles with the adhesive as needed.
4.9 Application method / tools - Application Notes.
    - Ensure all sheet joins and tapes etc are overlapped by 50mm.
    - Ensure all sheet joins and over laps are well bonded. If required the adhesive can be skimmed over sheet joins to protect sheet edges.
4.10 Cleaning of equipment. Tools and equipment can be clears with water prior to the adhesive setting.
4.11 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Not suitable for externally application over early aged concrete or screeds.
    - Not suitable for application with rising damp and high moisture related issues.
4.12 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Schonox AB Sheet membrane is designed as a complete system. Non propietory products use to fix the sheet shall be deem non-compliant.
    - Flood testing can be conducted at a 50mm maximum height after 24 hours at 23°C and 50% RH on porous substrates. (tested at 23°C and 50% relative humidity).
    - Please consult Sika for installations not mentioned in this document

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. Not below 5°C & not above 35°C
5.3 Substrate temperature. Not below 5°C & not above 35°C; Avoid application in hot direct sunlight ie >30°C as vapour pockets may occur. For external application in expose sun cover with screed or tile as soon as applicable or cover with a white corflute protection board or similar immediately after installation.
5.4 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.11):
    - Not suitable for application with rising damp and high moisture related issues.
    - Flood testing can be conducted at a 50mm maximum height after 24 hours at 23°C and 50% RH on porous substrates. (tested at 23°C and 50% relative humidity).
5.5 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.6 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SCHÖNOX® AB, October 2025, Version 01.08, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/k/schoenox_ab.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
